Fixation of support price of
Agricultural products by
States
*81.SHRI N. K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
decision to authorise the State
Governments to fix the support price of
Agricultural products which do not get the
expected price and the loss suffered would
be shared by the State Governments and
the Central Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have allotted
any amount to any State to sustain
the loss;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether Government propose to
allot any fund to Kerala for compensating
the loss of Support Price; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Policy for writing text books
*82.SHRI JIBON ROY: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news item appearing in
the Sunday Times of 28th October, 2001,
under the caption, "NCERT set to rewrite
unity in diversity" and
(b) whether Government would
announce a transparent policy on syllabus
making and the names who are selected for
writing text books?
Recruitment norms for Kendriya
Vidyalaya and Navodaya
Vidyalaya teachers
*83. DR. ARUN KUMAR
SARMA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPME NT be
pleased to state:
(a) the recruitment norms being
followed in selection of teachers for
Navodaya and Kendriya Vidyalayas,
including holding of written test, indicating
details of such tests held during the last
three years; and
(b) how the standardisation of results
of various universities is practiced for
rationality as well as to screen out the
product of fake universities?

Nutrition Fund
*84.SHRI B. J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a
decision for creation of a Nutrition Fund;
(b) if so, what is the allocation for the
Fund and how much has been spent so far in
different States;
(c) who is the target end user of this Fund;
and
(d) in what form this is going to reach the
target user?
B.G. line upto Rozi Peak and Bedi
Bunder in Gujarat
*85. SHRI BACHANI LEKHRAJ: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Gujarat Maritime had
paid necessary charges for final survey of
broad gauge line upto Rozi Peak and Bedi
Bunder;
(b) if so, the details of the survey; and
(c) by when the work is likely to
commence?
Production of cheaper urea
*86.SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that imported
urea is cheaper than that produced in our
country;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) what steps Government have taken
to make the production of urea cheaper in
the country?
Adverse impact of transfers in KVS
*87. SHRI RAMA SHANKER
KAUSHIK: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOP-
MENT be pleased to state:
(a) what is the transfer policy of
Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan;
(b) whether it is being implemented;
if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons
therefor;
(c) whether it is a fact that studies of
the children were adversely affected on
account of frequent transfers by the
administration during the last academic
session; and
(d) whether Government would issue
directives to stop unnecessary and before
time transfers; if so, by when and if not,
the reasons therefor?
ICAR Foot-and-Mouth Research
Centre in Kashmir
*88. PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM:  Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there was a proposal to
set up a Foot-and-Mouth Research
Centre in Kashmir by the Indian
Council for Agriculture Research;
if so, whether ICAR has set up the same;
and
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Doubling the track of  Konkan
Railways
*89. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) how many trains are run on the
Konkan Railways;

Filling up the post of D.G. ICAR
594. PROF. A. LAKSHMISAGAR:
SHRI  H.K. JAVARE GOWDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the post of D.G. ICAR has
been lying vacant since August last;
(b) whether there have been procedural
differences within ICAR about the
appointment of the DG to fill up the
vacancy;
(c) if so, what are the details thereof;
and
(d) what steps have been taken to
resolve the differences so as to fill up the
vacancy?
Growth of agriculture sector
595. SHRI B. J. PANDA : Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) what is the expected growth of
agriculture in terms of foodgrains in the
current financial year based on the
production estimate till date;
(b) what would be the expected growth
of agriculture including allied sector; and
(c) what has been the recommendations
of the Standing Committee of Chief
Ministers, with the Agriculture Minister
as convener for reforms in the Agriculture
sector?
Depression in A. P.
596. SHRI  RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI SOLIPETA RAMA-
CHANDRA REDDY:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of persons killed,
displaced and missing as a result of the
recent depression in the Bay of Bengal
district-wise in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the details of damage caused to
roads, bridges and other loss suffered in
the State; and
(c) the details of financial and other
assistance to be provided to Andhra
Pradesh Government in this regard?

131
WIN2\SESSION\3376rs 131
Scientists in Central Institute of
Fisheries Education
597. SHRI S. RAMACHANDRAN
PILLAI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether 41 per cent posts of
scientists in the Central Institute of Fisheries
Education, Mumbai were lying vacant as on
31st March, 2000 and the activities of the
Institute are hampered due to acute shortage
of scientists;
(b) whether the building work of the
deemed University planned in 1986 at a cost
of Rs. 6.67 crore has not commenced yet;
(c) whether against annual demand of 200
fisheries scientists, only 221 have passed
out from 1995 to 2000;
(d) if so, the reasons for these failures;
and
(e) what steps are being taken to remedy
these shortcomings?
Assistance to Himachal Pradesh for
natural calamities
598. SHRI ANIL SHARMA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) the estimated damage to human beings,
cattles and other properties caused by floods
and lightening that hit Himachal Pradesh
during the last three years, year-wise and
area-wise; and
(b) the details of financial assistance
extended by the Union Government by way
of loans, advances and grant for relief and
rehabilitation of the affected people in the
State?
Assistance to Southern States for
drought and fodder shortage
599. PROF. A. LAKSHMISAGAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the serious drought conditions and acute
shortage of fodder in Karnataka and other
Southern States; and
(b) if so, what is the nature of
assistance given by Government to
Karnataka Government so far to meet the
situation besides strengthening the fodder
bank and the fodder seed production?
Recommendations of Committee on
capital formation in Agriculture
600. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether an eight member expert
Committee on capital formation in
agriculture has been set up by Government
to look into the problem of drop in real
investment in this sector; and
(b) if so, what are the details thereof
and the recommendations of the
Committee, if any?
Horticulture Research Centre in
NER
601. SHRI W. ANGOU SINGH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of schemes formulated by
Government to set up Horticulture Research
Centre in North Eastern Region; and
(b) the details of amount spent on the
said schemes during the last three years?
Stopping the flow of terminator
seeds
602.  SHRI R. SARATH KUMAR:
  SHRI P.N. SIVA:
 Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken a

seeds into the Indian Market; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Strategy for crop diversification

’SURYA’: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal for
encouraging farmers to diversify from
traditional crops;
(b) if so, whether those crops have been
identified;
(c) whether any region-wise strategy
has been chalked out
